sources.citation: Olson, Kenneth S. 2013. A sketch of Lutos phonology. Handout, 43rd Colloquium on African Languages and Linguistics (CALL), Leiden, 26-28 August 2013. 8 pp. https://scholars.sil.org/sites/scholars/files/kenneth_s_olson/lutos/olsoncall2013handout.pdf
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. Sections: consonants, vowels, tone ('Three level tones: [V́], [V̄], [V̀]' with minimal sets), syllables, word patterns. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur (a full-text search for stress/accent = 0).
'Lutos has three tones: high, mid, low.' Nothing on stress (derived from Olson 2013).

sources.note: Describes the sister language Vale [vae], not Lutos (downloaded because same author, adjacent variety, mentions Luto/Nduga repeatedly). No stress/accent statement (a full-text search for stress/accent = 0).

sources.note: Nothing. Gives consonant systems of the Luto and Nduga dialects and notes a regular tonal correspondence (Nduga high-low : Luto high-superhigh); no mention of stress or accent.
